chapters.overview: Establishes the fundamental parameters of the Aryabhatan system. Defines the Mahayuga of 4,320,000 years, the precise number of revolutions for each planet, and encodes numbers using the Aryabhata alphabetic numeration system (Vargakshara and Avargakshara).

slokas.deva:
युगरविभगणाः ख्युघृ, शशि चयगियिङ्शुछ्लृ, कु ङिशिबुणॢष्खृ प्राक् ।
शनि ढुङ्विघ्व, गुरु ख्रिच्युभ, कुज भद्लिझ्नुखृ, भृगुबुधसौराः ॥
slokas.translit:
yugaravibhagaṇāḥ khyughṛ, śaśi cayagiyiṅśuchlṛ, ku ṅiśibuṇḷṣkhṛ prāk |
śani ḍhuṅvighva, guru khricyubha, kuja bhadlijhnukhṛ, bhṛgubudhasaurāḥ ||

anvaya.en: Sun's revolutions in a Yuga = khyughṛ (4,320,000)

slokas.translation: In a Yuga (4,320,000 solar years), the revolutions of the Sun are 4,320,000; of the Moon 57,753,336; of the Earth's daily rotations on its axis relative to the stars, 1,582,237,500.
slokas.source: editions/aryabhata-full-edition.html, verse १.१ (Devanāgarī, IAST and English as printed there)

formula.title: Earth's Sidereal Rotation vs Solar Year
formula.latex: \frac{\text{Earth Rotations}}{\text{Sun Revolutions}} = \frac{1582237500}{4320000} = 366.25868 \text{ sidereal days per year}
formula.notes: Aryabhata explicitly states the Earth rotates (Bhramana) relative to the fixed asterisms (Bha).

chapters.overview: Details Aryabhata's calculation of the 24 half-chord (Jya) differences, spherical trigonometry foundations, the formula for the area of a circle and triangle, and his famous extremely accurate approximation of Pi (π).

slokas.deva:
चतुरधिकं शतमष्टगुणं द्वाषष्टिस्तथा सहस्राणाम् ।
अयुतद्वयविष्कम्भस्यासन्नो वृत्तपरिणाहः ॥
slokas.translit:
caturadhikaṃ śatamaṣṭaguṇaṃ dvāṣaṣṭistathā sahasrāṇām |
ayutadvayaviṣkambhasyāsanno vṛttapariṇāhaḥ ||
slokas.translation: Add 4 to 100, multiply by 8, and then add 62,000. By this rule the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 20,000 can be approached.

formula.title: Aryabhata's Pi Approximation
formula.notes: Accurate to 4 decimal places. Aryabhata explicitly notes this is 'āsanna' (approximate), showing advanced understanding of irrationality.

chapters.codeSnippet:
def aryabhata_pi():
    circumference = (100 + 4) * 8 + 62000
    diameter = 20000
    return circumference / diameter
